issues.legal_issue: The duration of an interest in property is assessed by its availability from the date the interest vests, looking to present and future availability rather than past enjoyment.
material_facts: The assessments concerned whether the assessee’s interests in property were excluded from assets under the applicable wealth-tax definition.
The relevant statutory language referred to whether an interest “is available” for a specified period from the date it vests in the assessee.
issues.conclusion: The duration test concerns whether the interest is presently available and will remain available in the future for more than six years, measured from the date it vests in the assessee.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 2(e)(2)(iii) of the Wealth Tax Act, 1957, as substituted by the Finance Act, 1969, the words “is available” refer to present and future availability. The nature of the interest is assessed on the date it vests, rather than by the length of time it has already been enjoyed. The Court relied on Commissioner of Wealth Tax v. Smt. Muthukrishna Ammal, which construed the same duration language to ask how long the interest would remain available in the future; the 1964 amendment changed the relevant date to the date of vesting but did not change that construction.

predicates.wealth_tax_asset_classification_case: The proceeding determines whether an interest in property is an asset for wealth-tax purposes.
predicates.duration_test_uses_current_availability: The governing test describes the interest in terms of whether it is available for a stated period.
predicates.interest_vests_on_identifiable_date: The interest vests in the holder on an identifiable date.

issues.definition: When an asset-classification proceeding applies a duration test to an interest that vests on an identifiable date, the interest’s duration is measured forward from that date.

issues.legal_issue: A month-to-month tenancy that can be terminated at any time is not an asset where it is not shown to be available for more than six years from the date it vests.
material_facts: The original leases had expired, and the lessor had issued notices requiring the assessee to hand over vacant possession.
The assessee remained in possession under a new month-to-month tenancy for an unstated period.
The tenancy could be terminated by the lessor at any time by notice under Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act.
No fresh leases were shown to have been granted, although the assessee could seek them.
The properties generated rental income, but the Court considered the nature of the tenancy interest on the date it vested.
issues.conclusion: The tenancy interests were not assets within the applicable wealth-tax definition, and their value was not liable to be included in the assessee’s net wealth.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(e)(2)(iii) of the Wealth Tax Act, 1957, excludes an interest available for no more than six years from the date it vests. Sections 106 and 116 of the Transfer of Property Act govern the month-to-month tenancy arising after the expired leases and its termination by notice. Applying Commissioner of Wealth Tax v. Smt. Muthukrishna Ammal, the Court held that the tenancy’s precarious nature meant it could not be treated as available for more than six years from vesting; the absence of a termination notice did not make its future duration longer. A right to seek fresh leases did not establish that such leases had been granted or were available.

rule.if: wealth_tax_asset_classification_case and original_lease_expired and possession_continued_under_month_to_month_tenancy and tenancy_terminable_at_any_time and no_fresh_lease_granted

predicates.wealth_tax_asset_classification_case: The proceeding determines whether an interest in property is an asset for wealth-tax purposes.
predicates.original_lease_expired: The original lease under which the holder occupied the property had ended.
predicates.possession_continued_under_month_to_mont: After the original lease ended, the holder continued in possession under a month-to-month tenancy.
predicates.tenancy_terminable_at_any_time: The lessor could terminate the continuing tenancy at any time by giving notice.
predicates.no_fresh_lease_granted: No fresh lease was shown to have been granted to the holder.

issues.definition: When an original lease has ended and possession continues under a month-to-month tenancy that the lessor can terminate at any time, with no fresh lease granted, the tenancy interest is excluded from taxable assets.
